Sky class. Measures 16 horizon haze colour bins. Builds a PMREM environment from a copy whose ground is a flat sand bounce colour and whose sun is capped at 8. The visible background below the horizon is filled with each column's horizon colour and the sun capped at 40. apply(scene) sets background, environment, both rotations and the intensity. REUSE WITH CHANGES (constants are tied to this one file).

SunLight renders 2 cascades on every renderer.render. With 4 viewports (or 3 plus the overview) that is 8 shadow scene passes per frame, against 4 today. Whole-loop merged barriers and whole-track InstancedMeshes are never culled in those passes. Chunk everything (100-200 m) or use BatchedMesh, cap shadow.camera.far (around 120-150 m), and consider the existing single-box DirectionalLight path for the Low preset. The cascade count is hard-coded at 2 (SunLightShadow.js:42-44).

The one shared HDR target with scissored viewports breaks silently with shadows: after each shadow pass three restores viewport and scissor from renderTarget.viewport/.scissor/.scissorTest (WebGLRenderer.js:2954-2960). Set those fields per viewport, not renderer.setViewport/setScissor, or each view will draw over the whole target.

Removing the sea exposes the terrain edge. Terrain only reaches 380 m past the track bbox (world.ts:16), and FogExp2 at density 0.0013 is about 22% at 380 m. The overview camera (far 3000, high above) sees the edges directly. Needs a far ring, a dense tree belt, hills or a higher density. The below-horizon background is already horizon-coloured (sky.ts:89-95), which helps.

Terrain cost grows with a 3.3 km circuit. The heightAt grid took about 700 ms in Node for 49k points (TrackProximity ring search up to reach 160). A larger bbox could mean 150-200k points (several seconds on the main thread on the loading screen) and hundreds of 120 m chunks (draw calls per viewport). Precompute the heightfield in the trackgen build script, or use a worker, plus bigger/LOD chunks.

All placement and strip code assumes flat cross-sections and constant width (position + right*lateral, y = centre y). Trackgen banking or width overrides will make kerbs, run-off, barriers, scenery and terrain blend float or clip unless one banked helper is introduced and used everywhere.

Global ShaderChunk mutation (installHaze) plus baked constants: it must run before compileAsync, or precompiled programs will lack the haze. Changing the HDRI or sky means a different shader source. Any new onBeforeCompile material (rubber line, splat terrain, pine wind) needs customProgramCacheKey, or materials with identical closure source will share a program (Material.js:544-546).

Changing the light type (DirectionalLight vs SunLight) or shadow on/off between presets changes program defines, which means recompiles and hitches. Do it only between races (matches the 'drop one preset between races' rule) and precompile both variants if both can occur.

Visual and physics mismatch: today terrain is not a collider and invisible walls sit at halfDrivable+0.5 (trackGeometry.ts:81). With grass/gravel run-off, either the corridor loft owns the run-off surface (and terrain sits below it), or the terrain is drivable and its triangles must match the physics mesh and surface IDs exactly.
Naming clash: three's Sky addon and render/sky.ts both export Sky. The 'infield on the left' assumption (terrain.ts:61, 89; grandstand on -right, scenery.ts:274-278) flips if Track 1 runs clockwise.

Licence and packaging: anything placed in assets/ is publicly served and copied to dist (fine for the licence log and FAL credits, wasteful for raw XML). JSON cannot carry an FAL header comment, so use a '_licence' field, a sidecar text file or a .ts data module. Large generated data under client/src is checked by prettier format:check unless it is listed in .prettierignore.

The asset swap must stay commercially clean: only CC0 textures, HDRIs and models (Poly Haven, ambientCG, or own work), each recorded in ASSETS.md. ambientCG naming (Color/NormalGL/Roughness/AO as separate files) does not match loadPbrSet's Poly Haven _diff/_nor_gl/_arm convention, so pack an ARM texture or extend the loader.

JPG textures are decoded on the main thread and uploaded as RGBA8 with mipmaps (about 5.3 MB GPU each at 1k). Adding grass, gravel, forest floor, rubber mask and new asphalt sets raises GPU memory and load time. KTX2/Basis would need the transcoder WASM shipped in assets/.

CORNICHE_RUN: 26 control points, roadWidth 14, shoulderWidth 3.5, 8 checkpoints, startDistance 60, laps 3. Fully Corniche-specific. This is the file the trackgen output replaces.

Node-safe geometry from a Track. buildStrip makes a flat quad strip between two lateral offsets (n+1 rings, the closing ring reuses sample 0, UVs in metres/tile). drivableSurface is the physics strip from -halfDrivable to +halfDrivable. wallSegments makes yaw-only boxes every 4 samples. WALL_HEIGHT is 2.6. TrackProximity is a 24 m grid for nearest-sample lookups used by terrain and scenery.
buildTrackPhysics(physics, track): one trimesh for the drivable surface, wall boxes with friction 0.05, and a 4 km safety floor centred on the origin, 6 m below the lowest sample.
Corniche-specific test: length 1100-1300 m, minimumRadius > halfDrivable+1, 8 checkpoints, 4 grid cars grounded and inside halfRoad, and a full-lock drive into the wall stays within halfDrivable+0.5.

Fully Corniche-specific land height: SEA_LEVEL, CITY, COAST, beach, dunes and infield. It assumes an anticlockwise loop (infield on the left) and uses the scalar halfDrivable. Used by scene/terrainVisual.ts, scenery.ts, sea.ts, trackVisual.ts and world.ts. M8 replaces it.

PhysicsWorld wraps the Rapier world. SURFACE_FRICTION is {ground 0.9, wall 0.05}. Helpers: addBox (yaw only, friction combine Min), addConvexHull (currently unused), addTrimesh (FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES). staticColliders is never read outside this file.

Simulation: fixed 60 Hz step. Per step it runs car.prePhysics, world.step, car.postPhysics, then collects contact-force impacts. addCar(spawn) builds a Car from physics.rapier and physics.world. It knows nothing about surfaces.

Rapier ray-cast vehicle plus arcade assists. It has no track import. Its ground contact goes only through the wheel rays: frictionSlip and side stiffness are per wheel, so collider friction is not used for tyres (assumed; a test should confirm). It also holds item and boost code (boost, spinOut, push, spinTime) that M8 deletes, and draft (slipstream), which M8 keeps.
DriveInput {steer, throttle, brake, handbrake, horn}, NEUTRAL_INPUT, copyInput, mergeInputs. No track coupling.
Car feel tests on a flat addBox plane with no track. Any surface lookup must default to asphalt for unregistered colliders, or these tests change.
Collision and removal tests on a box plane. Not track dependent.

Race rules. Countdown hold, then gates in order (only the next gate counts). Gate 0 is the lap line. Ranking is finish time, then gates passed, then distance to the next gate. Also handles wrong way, respawn (flipped, stuck, off track; fade, then teleport to the last gate in the car's own lane) and insideGate.
Race tests on CORNICHE_RUN: countdown hold, a full 4-car 3-lap autopilot race (step cap 60*400, lap 25-75 s, 60 s timeout), and the gate-skip guard.

Ruudskogen replicates a real Norwegian circuit and does not close (10-30 m gap). Use g-track-2 (fictional, closes in 0.05 m) as the base and alter it with overrides. Any layout tweak breaks closure, so the closure solver (two adjustable straights plus one arc) is required, not optional.

Index-as-metres: if stations go to 0.5 m spacing, SAMPLE_SPACING (track.ts:56, used at :203), wallSegments (every 4), markings, barriers, kerbs, scenery spacing and the project window (40 samples, which would become ±20 m) all change silently. Walls are yaw-only boxes at the mean centre height (trackGeometry.ts:90). With banking up to 6-11° the low side's wall bottom can sit above the road edge, leaving a gap under the wall, and the tops step on grades. Build walls from the banked edge points (convex hulls or fully oriented boxes).

Crests: g-track-2's +7% then -3.5% at 'segment line 5-1/5b' would make cars airborne at 50 m/s (gravity 13) unless vertical curvature is limited. Airborne cars hurt autopilot tests, respawn (flipped) and feel.

Surface grip: Rapier's ray-cast vehicle most likely ignores collider friction for tyres, but the setWheelSideFrictionStiffness doc says it multiplies 'friction between a tire and the collider'. Confirm with a test, then apply grip through per-wheel setWheelFrictionSlip each step. Unknown colliders must map to asphalt, otherwise car.test.ts results shift.

Per-triangle lookup through castRayAndGetNormal featureId may return offset ids for back faces (parry). Per-surface colliders plus wheelGroundObject is safer, but FIX_INTERNAL_EDGES only fixes edges inside one collider. That is harmless for wheel rays; chassis contacts at surface seams need a check.
Respawn distance: with the current 'last gate + 3 m' rule and 8 gates on 3.2 km, a crash can send a car back up to 400 m. Use 16-20 gates and/or a last-safe-projection respawn.

Race test budget: 3 laps of about 3.2 km needs roughly 330-400 s simulated, against the cap of 24 000 steps (race.test.ts:51). Lap bounds at :66-67 fail as written. The autopilot (PLANNED_GRIP 15) may crash on crests or banking and stall the test.

Spawns are yaw-only and 0.5 m above the centre sample. On banked or graded grid spots, cars drop slightly and may rock; compute y on the banked cross-section.

Draw calls: chunking the corridor into 100-200 m pieces across 4-5 surface materials over 3.2 km means more than 100 meshes. With 4 viewports, merge per material per chunk and rely on frustum culling, or draw calls will eat the Low preset budget.

Floor and precision: the floor box is fixed at ±2000 m around the origin, and SD coordinates start at the start line (g-track-2 bbox x -448 to 712, y -315 to 443). Centre the generated track and size the floor from its bbox.
Lap records: changing TRACK_IDS affects server tests (router.test.ts:78-81, store.test.ts:113-126) and old rows. The 20 s minimum lap is too lax for 3.2 km (cheat or teleport laps).

g-track-2's 15 m road width and its pit straight (an as-pits side 15 m wide) are not club-circuit-like. Override the width (about 11-12 m) and treat the pits as decorative so they do not create a wide shortcut corridor.

XML parsing pitfalls: external entity &default-surfaces; tags inside comments; latin1 vs UTF-8; duplicate attributes; value inheritance across segments; % to fraction. A naive DOM parse or the sd_tracks.py sketch gets elevation, banking and sides wrong.

m8Changes.what: Canvas at DPR 1: always call webgl.setPixelRatio(1) and drop RENDER.maxPixelRatio (:52). Take a QualityPreset. Create a GpuTimer from this.webgl.getContext() as WebGL2RenderingContext. Keep antialias:false, depth:false and stencil:false (the composite needs no depth).
m8Changes.notes: With DPR 1, canvas px equal CSS px, so the HUD/layout rects (CSS px) map 1:1 to canvas px. On a 4K TV at macOS DPR 2 the browser does the final 2x upscale. Decide whether the sharpen pass also runs when devicePixelRatio>1 (recommended, since the browser upscale is bilinear and soft).

m8Changes.what: Replace with setLayout(rects) (integer canvas rects plus a padded tile atlas in the shared target), beginFrame(now), renderView(index, scene, camera, speed), endFrame(time), precompile(scene, camera) and a stats getter. beginFrame: gpuTimer.begin(), controller update, info.reset(). The canvas clear to SEAM_COLOUR (:74-76) goes away because the single composite writes every canvas pixel, seams included. endFrame: bloom once, composite once, then the optional upscale+RCAS, then gpuTimer.end().
m8Changes.notes: dispose(): also dispose the GpuTimer. Each race builds a new WebGLRenderer, so consider webgl.forceContextLoss() to free the context promptly.

m8Changes.what: One shared HDR target. Allocate sceneTarget once per preset at the MAX internal size: canvas px x the preset's internal-resolution cap (sizing knob maxInternalPixels), HalfFloat, samples = preset.msaa, storeMultisampledDepthBuffer:false, resolveDepthBuffer:false. Lay the viewports out as tiles whose origins are aligned to 2^bloomLevels px (16) with at least 16 px padding between them. Dynamic resolution renders a sub-rect of each tile (tile size x scale), so a scale change never reallocates. Per viewport: set target.viewport, target.scissor and target.scissorTest=true, then renderer.setRenderTarget(target), clear(), render(scene, camera).
m8Changes.notes: The viewport/scissor must be set on the TARGET before setRenderTarget. renderer.setViewport/setScissor are ignored for render targets, and shadowMap.render re-applies the target's own viewport/scissor when it restores the target (WebGLShadowMap.js:378).

m8Changes.what: Run the bloom chain once per frame over the used region of the shared target, not once per viewport. Add uniform vec4 uTiles[4] (uv min/max of each tile at the current scale) and int uTileCount. Clamp every tap to the containing tile, inset by half a texel. Write 0 in the padding. Limit each mip pass to the used region via the mip target's viewport/scissor. BLOOM_LEVELS comes from the preset.
m8Changes.notes: This keeps the old 'bloom never bleeds across seams' guarantee (DECISIONS.md:138-139). Cost at 4 viewports drops from 28 bloom passes to 7.

m8Changes.what: One fullscreen composite per frame. Uniform arrays: uRects[4] (canvas px), uTileXform[4] (offset/scale into target uv, including the dynamic scale), uSpeed[4], uAspect[4], int uCount, uSeamColour. Each fragment finds its viewport and computes local uv, so vignette and speed lines stay per viewport. Fragments outside every rect get the seam colour. Bloom and grade stay as they are.
m8Changes.notes: Without upscaling, the composite writes the canvas directly and keeps the dither. With upscaling, it writes an LDR RGBA8 target at internal resolution in canvas layout, and the dither moves to the final pass.

m8Changes.what: Add an LDR target and a GLSL RCAS ShaderMaterial (5-tap contrast-adaptive sharpen; bilinear or a light EASU-style upscale). It runs when the internal size is smaller than the canvas, and optionally when DPR>1. Taps clamp to the viewport rect. Sharpness is set per preset (RCAS units: 0 = max, 2 = none; about 0.2-0.5). Dither and the final sRGB-encoded output happen here.
m8Changes.notes: No GLSL CAS exists in three r186. Port the math from examples/jsm/tsl/display/SharpenNode.js or FSR1Node.js (TSL, MIT) into the existing ShaderMaterial style.

m8Changes.what: Replace the fps trigger with a GPU-time controller. Input is the gpuMs from the GpuTimer (median of the last ~10 results). Target budget about 12-13.5 ms at 60 Hz, derived from the measured refresh. Scale steps are multiplicative and quantised (e.g. 0.05) between preset.minScale and 1. Drop at once when over budget; raise only after ~2-3 s under budget with hysteresis. At most one change per ~250-500 ms. Fallback when no timer is available: missed-vsync detection from raw rAF deltas against the measured refresh interval, never fixed 55/58 fps thresholds.
m8Changes.notes: Keep enabled/reset() for the R debug key (game.ts:426-431). With sub-rect rendering the R toggle no longer needs layout().

m8Changes.what: Wrap EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 in a ring of 3-4 WebGLQuery. begin() runs before the first draw of the frame (including the shadow passes) and end() after the last post pass. poll() is non-blocking and checks QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE. When GPU_DISJOINT_EXT is set, drop all pending results. supported=false falls back to CPU timing.
m8Changes.notes: Declare the extension interface locally, because TS 6.0.3 lib.dom lacks it, and cast getExtension's any result to satisfy strictTypeChecked eslint. TIME_ELAPSED queries cannot nest. three's WebGLRenderer issues no queries itself, so one frame-wide query is safe.

m8Changes.what: Define PRESETS high/medium/low: maxInternalPixels or scale cap, minScale, msaa (4/4/2 or 0+FXAA), shadowMapSize per cascade (2048/1536/1024), shadowFar (cascade range, e.g. 200/150/100 m), bloomLevels (4/4/3), anisotropy (8/8/4), sharpness, vegetationDensity/drawDistance. choosePreset(playerCount): 1 player High, 2 Medium, 3-4 Low. Then the loading benchmark may drop it one step, and the result of the previous race may drop it one step (between races only).
m8Changes.notes: Each race mounts a new SplitWaysGame and WebGLRenderer: the Stage unmounts on lobby (TvApp.tsx:85-91; hub phases lobby/playing/results, hub.ts:142-154,325-329). So the between-race preset memory must be module-level in render/quality.ts (optionally sessionStorage), not on the renderer.

m8Changes.what: Allocation-free rolling stats: a ring buffer or fixed-bucket histogram of raw rAF deltas, CPU frame ms and GPU ms. Provides p50, p99, missed frames (delta > 1.5x refresh), refreshHz estimate, and 30-minute soak totals. Used by the overlay, the benchmark and telemetry.
m8Changes.notes: Replaces game.ts trackFps (:684-691) and fps/frames/fpsWindowStart/lastFrameMs (:157-160).

m8Changes.what: Switch to SunLight from three/examples/jsm/lights/SunLight.js: position = sunDirection x distance, castShadow, shadow.mapSize and shadow.camera.far from the preset, radius/bias/normalBias retuned. Remove focus() and both sun.focus calls, because the cascades refit to whichever camera renders, inside each renderer.render().
m8Changes.notes: 2 cascades means 2 shadow atlas passes per render() call, so 8 shadow passes per frame at 4 viewports versus 4 today. Low can keep the current DirectionalLight focus approach if the benchmark demands it. The light type must be fixed before precompile because it changes the shader programs.

facts: Frame flow today (game.ts:557-649, renderer.ts:68-82, postProcessing.ts:250-274). beginFrame: optional resolution change, info.reset, full-canvas clear to 0x050608. For each viewport: camera.update(aspect = rect aspect), sun.focus(car), then post.render, which binds sceneTarget (whole target, scissorTest false), clears, renders the scene (shadow map + scene + MSAA resolve inside), runs bloom (1 prefilter + 3 downsample + 3 additive upsample = 7 passes), sets the canvas viewport/scissor to the rect and draws the composite. The 3-player overview cell repeats this with sun.focus(overview.focus) (:642-648). The podium renders one full-canvas view (:565-568).

At 4 viewports one frame has 4 shadow-map renders, 4 scene renders, 4 full-target MSAA resolves, 28 bloom passes, 4 composite draws and 1 canvas clear. DECISIONS.md:161 reports 481 draw calls per frame at 4 players.

The HDR targets are sized to ONE viewport: rects[0] (or the full canvas on the podium) x DPR (<=1.25) x resolution.scale (game.ts:452-454, renderer.ts:64-66, :89-92). All viewports reuse them one after another.

MSAA: sceneTarget = WebGLRenderTarget(HalfFloatType, samples RENDER.msaaSamples=4, depthBuffer true, stencil false, resolveDepthBuffer false) (postProcessing.ts:153-161,164; config.ts:170). The canvas context has antialias:false and depth:false (renderer.ts:30-36).

Tone mapping and colour space are manual: renderer.toneMapping=NoToneMapping (renderer.ts:39), and the composite does ACES (Hill fit), manual toSrgb and an 8-bit dither (postProcessing.ts:135-143). renderer.outputColorSpace=SRGB has no effect on the composite ShaderMaterial.

Dynamic resolution today is fps-based (dynamicResolution.ts:45-63) and changes the scale in 0.1 steps between 0.6 and 1. Each change calls post.setSize, then RenderTarget.setSize, which disposes and reallocates the MSAA, bloom and scene GPU resources (postProcessing.ts:234-244; three core/RenderTarget.js setSize calls this.dispose()). That causes a hitch.
The fps thresholds 55/58 assume 60 Hz. On a 50 Hz or 30 Hz TV mode, fps stays under 55 and the scale sinks to minScale for good (dynamicResolution.ts:46-52).

Precompile does not exist today: the loop starts inside the constructor (game.ts:299-303), before the Stage hides its loading overlay (SplitWaysStage.tsx:151-164). Shaders compile synchronously on the first frames.

compileAsync exists (WebGLRenderer.js:1515-1574). It calls compile() and then polls program.isReady() every 10 ms, without blocking when KHR_parallel_shader_compile is available (:1555). compile() gathers lights with traverseVisible plus a camera layer test, and prepares materials of every Mesh/Points/Line/Sprite via scene.traverse, so hidden objects are included (:1408-1490). It does not compile WebGLShadowMap depth materials or materials that only post passes draw.

Program cache keys depend on the bound render target: toneMapping and outputColorSpace switch when a target is bound (WebGLPrograms.js:121,177-183,213). Precompile must run with the HDR target bound to match the real scene passes.

Per-target viewport/scissor: setRenderTarget(target) copies target.viewport, target.scissor and target.scissorTest into GL state (WebGLRenderer.js:2934 +21-27, +108-110). Only the canvas path uses renderer.setViewport/setScissor (x pixelRatio). shadowMap.render runs inside every render() (WebGLRenderer.js:1737) and finishes with setRenderTarget(currentRenderTarget) (WebGLShadowMap.js:378), which re-applies the target's viewport/scissor.

The MSAA resolve after every render() into a target blits the FULL target (0,0,w,h) (WebGLTextures.js:2342) and then invalidates the multisampled colour attachment (WebGLTextures.js:2360). The GLES3 blit is scissor-tested, so with target.scissorTest=true each viewport's resolve only touches its own tile. One viewport's scene must never be split across two render() calls into the MSAA target.

Shadow maps follow the view camera: WebGLShadowMap.render calls shadow.updateMatrices(light, camera) with the view camera (WebGLShadowMap.js:291). SunLightShadow fits its 2 cascades to that camera each call, so one SunLight serves every viewport without focus() calls.

SunLight in three r186 is WebGL-native: WebGLLights handles 'SunLight' (WebGLLights.js:26,102,289,566), and WebGLProgram has NUM_SUN_LIGHTS/NUM_SUN_LIGHT_SHADOWS. Range = min(shadow.camera.far (500), viewCamera.far).

This repo uses the default, so it is inactive. It is a poor fit anyway: one full-canvas target with fixed 4x MSAA and nothing per viewport.

risks: Apple M1 is a tile-based GPU (ANGLE on Metal). Every viewport's render() breaks the HDR render pass, because the shadow map renders in between and there is a scissored clear plus the resolve blit. With a 4x MSAA half-float target, each break can mean loading and storing the attachment (about 66 MB per pass at 1080p internal). Measure with the benchmark. Mitigations: storeMultisampledDepthBuffer:false; msaa 2 or 0+FXAA on Low; pre-render all shadow maps before the scene passes via renderer.shadowMap.render([light_i], scene, camera_i) with shadowMap.autoUpdate=false and one light per viewport selected by light.layers.

SunLight doubles shadow passes (2 fixed cascades): 8 per frame at 4 viewports versus 4 today. The cascade count cannot be changed without forking the shader chunks. Fallback for Low: keep the current DirectionalLight with texel-snapped focus, or the CSM addon. The choice must be made before precompile.

EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 is not guaranteed on the reference device. Safari does not expose it, and on Chrome/macOS (ANGLE Metal) it must be verified on the M1. Results arrive 1-3 frames late and can be discarded on GPU_DISJOINT. On a tile-based GPU, TIME_ELAPSED may be coarse. Telemetry must record whether the timer was available, and the controller needs a robust CPU/rAF fallback.

The 'p99 frame time < 16.7 ms' criterion cannot be met if measured as raw rAF deltas at 60 Hz, because timestamp jitter alone produces deltas just over 16.7 ms. Define it in the spec as GPU ms and CPU ms p99 under budget plus a missed-vsync rate (delta > 1.5x refresh), and record the refresh rate. A 4K TV over an HDMI adapter may run at 30 Hz or 50 Hz.

Shared-target pitfalls: viewport/scissor must be set on the render target, not the renderer. scissorTest must stay true during render() so the full-size MSAA resolve blit (WebGLTextures.js:2342) is clipped to the tile, and the MSAA colour is invalidated after every resolve (:2360). A second render() into the same tile in one frame would read undefined MSAA data.
Bloom mips over a shared target bleed across tiles unless tiles are aligned and padded to 2^levels px and taps are clamped per tile. The old per-viewport pipeline got this for free.

Memory: a shared 4x MSAA RGBA16F target at 1920x1080 is about 66 MB colour, 33 MB depth and 17 MB resolved, plus bloom and LDR. At 4K internal it is about 4x that. Cap internal pixels per preset, independent of output size.

Dynamic resolution through RenderTarget.setSize reallocates GPU memory and hitches. The new controller must render sub-rects of a target allocated at maximum size, and setSize must only happen on preset or layout changes.

compileAsync coverage gaps: shadow depth materials, post ShaderMaterials, podium scene programs, and objects or material variants created later (new InstancedMesh counts do not matter; a new material/define combination does). Warm-up frames behind the loading overlay plus a renderer.info.programs check are needed. Changing light types, shadowMap.type or fog after precompile invalidates the programs.

A new WebGL context per race can pile up contexts (Chrome warns past about 16) and repeats shader compilation every race. Consider forceContextLoss on dispose, or keeping one module-level renderer across races.

The between-race preset drop must survive Stage unmount: store it in a module-level singleton or sessionStorage. The loading benchmark must not run the physics step or the race countdown, so loop.start() has to move out of the constructor.
Switching Track 1 from the HDRI to the analytic r186 Sky breaks Sky.hazeColours (measured from HDRI pixels) and the PMREM environment path unless replaced with fromScene and a readback.

Fixing the car shadow proxy restores car shadows but adds draw calls: 1 per car per shadow pass, x2 with cascades. Option (a) also adds 1 invisible draw per car per viewport. Budget for it in the draw-call targets.
The TSL generators and sharpen/FSR nodes import three/webgpu. Importing them by accident pulls the WebGPU build into the client bundle and may break the production build size budget.

files.role: The only API dispatcher. createApiHandler() builds a route key `${method} ${pathname without trailing slash}` and switches on literal strings ('POST /api/room', 'GET /api/room', 'POST /api/signal', 'GET /api/signal', 'POST /api/laps', 'GET /api/laps'). It validates with zod through parse(), which returns a generic 400. It maps RoomStatus to 404/403, turns HttpError into a JSON error response, and anything else into a 500. HttpError(status, message). readJsonBody(req) streams the body with a hard 32 KiB cap (413), returns {} for an empty body, returns 400 for invalid JSON, and ignores Content-Type. sendJson(res, status, body) always sends no-store. requestOrigin(req) honours the x-forwarded-* headers.

Integration test: a real node:http server on port 0 wrapping createApiHandler, with a PGlite store and readEnv({TURN_*}). It calls the API with global fetch and covers room creation and ICE, signal validation/routing (400/401/404) and the leaderboard (200 / 400 for an unknown track). It hardcodes 'corniche-run'.

Vercel function entry, the default export handler(req,res). Returns 500 when DATABASE_URL is missing. Lazily builds one ApiHandler per warm instance with a Neon runner and padOrigin=requestOrigin. Routing goes through router.ts, so no per-route code is needed here.

ServerEnv { databaseUrl, iceServers, publicUrl } built by readEnv(source=process.env) from DATABASE_URL, TURN_URL/TURN_USER/TURN_PASS and PUBLIC_URL. This is the place for an optional telemetry kill-switch env var.

Local servers for `pnpm dev` and `pnpm start`. createLocalContext() loads .env, uses Neon if DATABASE_URL is set and in-memory PGlite otherwise, and wires createApiHandler with the LAN https padOrigin and a terminal QR. createLocalServers() sends every `/api/` URL prefix to the API on both http:4000 and https:4443. New routes need no registration here.
`pnpm dev`: Vite middleware plus createLocalServers. No route knowledge.
`pnpm start`: serves client/dist plus the API through createLocalServers. No route knowledge.

Store interface and createStore(sql). Every method runs one batch (one Neon HTTP transaction): CLEANUP (expire rooms/signals), then touch(room) RETURNING host_key, then the statement. Status comes from roomStatus(results.at(-2), key). run() creates the schema lazily on Postgres error 42P01 and retries. postTelemetry goes here.
SCHEMA: SqlQuery[] with CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS for rooms, signals and laps. Used both by lazy creation in store.run() and by `pnpm db:migrate`. The telemetry table and indexes go here.
SqlQuery {text, params}, Row, SqlRunner.batch(queries): Promise<Row[][]> (runs in order, in one transaction), q(text, ...params), isMissingTableError (code 42P01).
createNeonRunner(url): uses @neondatabase/serverless neon() over HTTPS. A single query runs as sql.query; several run as sql.transaction.
createPgliteRunner(): an in-memory WASM Postgres with the same SQL, each batch in db.transaction. Used by local dev without DATABASE_URL and by all server tests.
`pnpm db:migrate`: loads .env and runs SCHEMA on Neon. Covers the new table automatically once it is in SCHEMA.

Store unit tests on a fresh PGlite per test (beforeEach): room codes and keys, signal delivery order, host-key enforcement, inbox cap, 10-minute expiry (via a raw UPDATE through runner.batch), and best lap per driver. Hardcodes 'corniche-run'.

zod contracts for /api/*: ROOM_* constants, peerId/hostKey/session schemas, signal payloads, create/room-info responses, postSignalRequestSchema, TRACK_IDS=['corniche-run'], trackIdSchema, postLapsRequestSchema, leaderboard schemas, apiErrorSchema. The telemetry request schema goes here.

facts: Routing is one string switch. router.ts:58 builds `${req.method ?? 'GET'} ${url.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '')}`, cases are at :61, :74, :86, :99, :108 and :115, and the default returns 404 'Not found' at :122-123. Adding a route means adding one case; local servers need no registration (local/server.ts:76 sends any URL starting with '/api/' to the API).

Vercel deploys one function. build-vercel.mjs bundles server/src/vercel.ts into functions/api/room.func (:21-37) and symlinks each other entry of API_ROUTES = ['room','signal','laps'] (:13-14, :54-56). config.json has `{ handle: 'filesystem' }` followed by `{ src: '^/api/.*$', status: 404 }` (:69-71), so any /api path without a .func alias returns 404 in production. The existing .vercel/output/functions/api/ confirms this layout: laps.func -> room.func, signal.func -> room.func.

The function config is runtime nodejs22.x, launcherType Nodejs, shouldAddHelpers false and maxDuration 10 (build-vercel.mjs:40-53). The bundle is CJS with a footer that re-exports the default (:33-35).
vercel.ts:16-19 returns 500 when DATABASE_URL is not set. vercel.ts:20-24 builds the handler lazily once per warm instance with createNeonRunner.
readJsonBody caps bodies at 32 KiB (http.ts:3, :20 returns 413), returns {} for an empty body (:23), returns 400 for invalid JSON (:27) and never checks Content-Type (http.ts:14-29).

router.ts parse() discards zod issues and always returns 400 'Invalid request' (router.ts:38-42). Unknown HttpErrors become a JSON {error} response with their status; any other error is logged and becomes 500 (:125-132).

Each Store method sends one batch, which is one transaction and one HTTP round trip on Neon (sql.ts:10, neon.ts:13-15, pglite.ts:12). The pattern is [...CLEANUP, touch(room), statement], with status from results.at(-2) (store.ts:109-128, :158-172).

CLEANUP runs on every room, signal and laps call except leaderboard. It deletes rooms idle longer than ROOM_TTL_SECONDS=600 and signals older than 120 s (store.ts:37-40, shared/src/api.ts:12). There is no cron.

Lazy schema: store.run() catches only 42P01 (missing table), runs the full SCHEMA, then retries (store.ts:72-81, sql.ts:19-21). All SCHEMA statements use IF NOT EXISTS (schema.ts:10-34), so adding a new table is safe for deployed databases.
laps has no FK to rooms and stores room as plain text (schema.ts:27-33). signals cascades from rooms (schema.ts:19). The telemetry table should follow laps (no FK).

postLaps requires the host key: INSERT ... WHERE EXISTS (rooms WHERE code=$1 AND host_key=$2) (store.ts:162-165). postSignal returns 'inbox-full' when the guarded insert returns no rows after the room checks passed (store.ts:126-128). This is the template for 'rate-limited'.

There is no rate limiting anywhere in the server except the per-peer signal inbox cap MAX_PENDING_SIGNALS=64 (store.ts:19, :116). POST /api/room is unauthenticated (router.ts:61-72), so anyone can mint a room and host key.

TV credentials: hub.roomCredentials() (hub.ts:128-130) delegates to hostTransport.credentials() (hostTransport.ts:111-113). hostTransport.poll() replaces the room on 404/403 (hostTransport.ts:175-180).

The TV polls /api/signal every 1000 ms in lobby and results and every 2000 ms while playing (hub.ts:57, hostTransport.ts:185). That keeps the room's last_seen fresh, so a host-key-gated telemetry post stays valid through a 30-minute soak.

The client request() spreads init, so keepalive passes through, and it sets content-type only when there is a body (client/src/net/api.ts:26-31). An existing sendBeacon usage is beaconSignal (api.ts:70-75), used by padTransport on pagehide (padTransport.ts:66, :246).
shared/src/index.ts:1-2 re-exports protocol and api. Server and client import everything from '@gamergang/shared'.

zod is 4.6.5 in shared and server (shared/package.json:12, server/package.json:11). Verified at runtime: z.object strips unknown keys, z.strictObject rejects them, and z.number() rejects Infinity and NaN.

TS config: strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax (so import types with `import type`), noUnusedLocals/Parameters (tsconfig.base.json). ESLint uses strictTypeChecked plus consistent-type-imports (eslint.config.js:11-21).

vitest picks up '**/src/**/*.test.ts' (vitest.config.ts:5). The baseline server suite passes 9 tests in about 27 s (run locally: `npx vitest run server`). Both suites use PGlite: store.test.ts creates a fresh DB per test (:14-17); router.test.ts runs a real http server on port 0 with one DB per file (:14-24).

SELECT FROM jsonb_array_elements($6::jsonb) with an EXISTS(host_key) guard and room and global count caps inserts 2+2 rows, then refuses the third post (room cap 5). risks: Missing Vercel alias. If 'telemetry' is not added to API_ROUTES (build-vercel.mjs:13), production returns 404 through the catch-all at :71, while pnpm dev, pnpm start and every vitest test pass. Add a guard test that checks the router cases against API_ROUTES.

Room and key gating does not prevent abuse on its own. POST /api/room is unauthenticated (router.ts:61), so an attacker can mint unlimited rooms and keys and post up to the per-room cap from each. The global hourly row cap in the INSERT is the real circuit breaker. An in-memory limiter in the function is unreliable across Vercel instances and cold starts, and there is no KV or Redis. Vercel WAF rate-limit rules are an optional extra layer (plan availability not verified).

Neon storage and compute on the free tier. A worst case of 2000 rows/hour at ~1-2 KB/row with 90-day retention could exceed 0.5 GB. Keep the global cap conservative, keep frameHistogram optional and small, or shorten retention. Each telemetry POST is an extra Neon round trip and can wake a suspended compute.

The lazy schema only handles missing tables (42P01, sql.ts:19-21). If telemetry columns are added later, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS will not add them, and inserts fail with 42703. Future changes need `ALTER TABLE telemetry ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ...` in SCHEMA plus `pnpm db:migrate`. Keeping most fields in jsonb `sample` avoids this.

A concurrent first use of an empty database can race two CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in parallel transactions (a pg_type unique violation, 23505). This is an existing low-probability issue, and adding a table slightly widens it. Running `pnpm db:migrate` once against Neon after deploy removes it.

Privacy and commercial use. The user agent, the GPU renderer string (WEBGL_debug_renderer_info), the screen size and the DPR together form a fingerprint. Do not store IP addresses or player names, document the collected fields (README/DECISIONS), and consider an opt-out. Do not add an unauthenticated GET that returns telemetry.

sendBeacon returns false when over the keepalive quota (~64 KiB in flight, shared with fetch keepalive), and its response cannot be read, so 4xx errors (400 schema drift, 403, 429) are silent. Use fetch with keepalive for benchmark posts and beacon only on pagehide. Keep payloads well under 16 KiB (8 samples).

Schema drift between client and server. The response is a generic 400 with no details (router.ts:38-42), so mismatches are hard to debug. Consider a console.warn of zod issue paths in non-production, or log result.error.issues server-side.

zod rejects NaN and Infinity. fps or gpu values from empty windows, or a divide by zero, make the whole POST fail. The client must clamp values and use null when the GPU timer is unavailable. EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 is missing on Safari and some configurations, so gpuMs* must be nullable, with gpuTimeSource recording the fallback.

Credentials can change mid-session (hostTransport.ts:175-180 recreates the room on 404/403, e.g. after the laptop sleeps). Telemetry must read hub.roomCredentials() at send time. A room code can also be reused by another TV after expiry, so group analysis by the client-generated `session`, not by `room`.

Telemetry is not persisted when the benchmark runs locally without DATABASE_URL (PGlite in memory, local/server.ts:35). The owner's M1 benchmark must run against the Vercel deployment, or locally with DATABASE_URL set in .env.

If the fly-through benchmark runs on a page or route that does not start the hub/hostTransport (and so never creates a room), there are no credentials and the post is impossible. Either run the benchmark inside the normal /tv flow or have it call api.createRoom() first.

m8Changes.notes: `class SteerProcessor { value = 0; process(raw: number, dt: number): number; reset(): void }` = shapeSteer(raw, STEER_INPUT.deadZone 0.05, STEER_INPUT.gamma 1.5), then a one-pole low-pass with tau = STEER_INPUT.lowPassSeconds 0.04 (alpha = 1 - exp(-dt/tau)). Give each Driver one, run it in step() right after mergeInputs (489) on the merged car.input.steer and before race.holdInputs (493), so holds still override. Reset it on respawn. car.applySteering already does the speed-sensitive lock (0.58 rad at ≤6 m/s down to 0.17 rad at ≥44 m/s, smoothstep) and a road-wheel rate limit: re-express STEERING.turnRate 3.4 rad/s (~195°/s) / returnRate 5.5 rad/s (~315°/s) as turnRateDegPerS 150 (spec 120-180) / returnRateDegPerS ~240 (research notes) and convert in applySteering. Autopilot (474-482) bypasses the processor by design. Keyboard ±1 goes through it too: gamma does nothing on ±1, but the low-pass and rate limit smooth it. Optionally reuse rampSteer for keyboard keys so they feel like Buttons.

facts: Input message: {type:'input', steer:-1..1, throttle:0..1, brake:0..1, handbrake:boolean, horn:boolean, t:number} validated by zod (shared/src/protocol.ts:94-102). JSON payloads over 4096 chars are dropped (protocol.ts:264).

Input travels on a pre-negotiated unordered channel with no retransmits (client/src/net/rtc.ts:31-36). PadTransport.send routes type 'input' there and everything else over the reliable 'state' channel (client/src/net/padTransport.ts:85). The TV only sends on the reliable channel (client/src/net/hostTransport.ts:115-120).

Send rate: the rAF tick calls InputSender.update every frame (SplitWaysController.tsx:169-209). It sends at most every 33.3 ms when something changed (inputSender.ts:6, 31) and repeats every 100 ms when nothing changed (inputSender.ts:11). Steer changes under 0.015 don't count (inputSender.ts:13), and steer is rounded to 3 dp (inputSender.ts:33).
Today throttle and brake are digital 0/1 from held zones (SplitWaysController.tsx:188-189), but the schema already allows analog 0..1 (protocol.ts:97-98).

The hub accepts input only from inGame players in phase 'playing' and drops any message whose t is <= the last t from that peer, because the channel is unordered (hub.ts:225-233). lastInputTime is cleared when the peer closes (hub.ts:197), and a new offer from a known pad closes the old link first (hostTransport.ts:194), so a reloaded pad (performance.now restarts) is not blocked.
t is the phone's rAF timestamp (SplitWaysController.tsx:169, 185-193) and not a sequence number.

Coast rule: each physics step a car uses its pad input only while driver.connected && now - padInputAt < INPUT.staleAfterMs (600 ms); otherwise NEUTRAL_INPUT (game.ts:483-484, config.ts:144-147). Pad and keyboard are merged as max |steer|, max throttle/brake, OR of booleans (sim/input.ts:31-42, game.ts:489).

Link liveness: the TV pings every 1000 ms (hub.ts:92-95, rtc.ts:14). The pad answers pong on the reliable channel (padTransport.ts:166-169). Both sides drop a link after 5000 ms of silence (rtc.ts:13, padTransport.ts:215-221, hostTransport.ts:300-308). The pad reconnects with backoff min(5000, 400*2^n) ms (padTransport.ts:237). A disconnected in-game driver is marked not connected (game.ts:330-333) and its HUD shows 'Reconnecting...' (game.ts:677).
Pad safety: on visibilitychange all held pointers are cleared so gas can't stick (SplitWaysController.tsx:213-217). rAF stops when the tab hides, so the TV coasts the car after 600 ms.

Current modes: tilt (default, profile.ts:20) uses TiltSteering on deviceorientation (steering.ts:67-97). Full lock is at 38° with a 2° dead zone (steering.ts:4-6, 39-47) and 35 ms exponential smoothing (steering.ts:8, 84-87). The wheel graphic shows the raw angle clamped to ±120° (SplitWaysController.tsx:197). Buttons uses rampSteer: 0→1 in 0.15 s, back in 0.1 s, straight through centre when flipping (steering.ts:10-11, 50-57). Both held = 0.

Tilt layout: handbrake + brake on the left, wheel with the horn on its hub in the centre, item-or-horn + gas on the right (SplitWaysController.tsx:246-268). Buttons layout: arrows on the left half, handbrake/item/horn plus brake/gas on the right half (270-297).

iOS motion flow: the JOIN tap (PadApp.tsx:68-76) synchronously calls requestTiltPermission() (device.ts:25-33; 'unsupported' without DeviceOrientationEvent or on non-https, 'granted' when there is no requestPermission i.e. Android). verifyTilt (PadApp.tsx:53-64) then waits for probeTiltSensor (1500 ms for a non-null beta/gamma, device.ts:36-49). On failure it switches the profile to buttons with a note (tiltFallbackNote 25-31). Fullscreen is skipped whenever requestPermission exists (PadApp.tsx:70). In-race, if tilt has no reading 900 ms after mount, a full-screen 'Tap to enable wheel' button calls onEnableTilt → changeMode('tilt') → requestTiltPermission again (SplitWaysController.tsx:110, 174-180, 315-328; PadApp.tsx:153).

Haptics: TV→pad 'haptic' patterns collision/start/finish/pickup/hit (protocol.ts:224-227), mapped to navigator.vibrate patterns (device.ts:84-94); iOS Safari has no Vibration API. The TV sends 'start' on green (game.ts:234-236) and 'finish' per racer (237-241). It sends 'collision' when impact force > CAR.mass*40 (game.ts:109), at most every 350 ms (game.ts:106, 525-528), and 'pickup'/'hit' only from items (game.ts:370, 383). Local pad buzzes: 8 ms on entering a zone (SplitWaysController.tsx:150) and 12 ms on item use (130).

Wake lock: keepScreenAwake() is called only from the JOIN tap (PadApp.tsx:71). It requests navigator.wakeLock 'screen' if available and re-requests on visibilitychange→visible (device.ts:65-82). The Wake Lock API needs a secure context, which is why the LAN server serves https to phones (server/src/local/server.ts:39, cert.ts:11).

Reverse today is instant: in Car.applyDrive, if brake > 0 && throttle === 0 && forwardSpeed < BRAKES.reverseBelowSpeed (0.8 m/s), the engine force becomes -brake*ENGINE.reverseForce(6000)*falloff toward reverseTopSpeed 11 m/s; otherwise brake = brake*BRAKES.impulse (car.ts:389-397, config.ts:67-68, 80). Reversing turns off brake-oversteer (car.ts:422-430). There is no reverse state outside that function.

Steering on the TV (car.ts:367-377): max road-wheel angle = lerp(0.58, 0.17 rad, smoothstep(|v|, 6, 44 m/s)), target = -steer*maxAngle, rate-limited at 3.4 rad/s turning further and 5.5 rad/s returning (config.ts:83-92). That is a speed-sensitive lock plus a road-wheel rate limit, with no dead zone, curve or low-pass on the TV.

Item spin-out overrides car input with neutral + handbrake (car.ts:227-231). race.holdInputs zeroes input during the countdown (with handbrake), after finishing (light brake) and during respawn fade-out (race.ts:100-111). It runs after the pad/keyboard merge (game.ts:489-493).

Auto-respawn: flipped > 3 s, or stuck > RESPAWN.stuckSeconds (3 s), where stuck = (throttle > 0.3 || brake > 0.3) && |v|² < 1, or off track; it fades out 0.3 s, teleports to the last gate in the car's lane and fades in 0.45 s (race.ts:196-229, 241-255, config.ts:139). There is no manual reset.

Reliable one-shots: pad store.action(a) → {type:'action'} on the reliable channel (padStore.ts:89-91) → hub forwards only for inGame+playing (hub.ts:221-224) → SplitWaysGame.handleAction → actions[a](driverIndex) (game.ts:320-328). The only action today is 'item'.

Keyboard: two key sets (A/D/W/S/Space/E/Q and arrows/RShift/Slash/Enter), digital ±1 steer that relies on the car's rate limit for smoothing (keyboard.ts:14-33, 47, 63-73). With no keyboard players, WASD also drives car 0 (game.ts:253).

Race status goes to each pad at 5 Hz on the reliable channel (game.ts:105, 304, 723-753) and immediately on item changes (game.ts:371, 377). The pad uses it for its HUD, countdown and finished overlays (SplitWaysController.tsx:28-46, 225-226, 310-334).

Pointer handling: setPointerCapture on the root <main> when pointerdown hits a [data-zone] (SplitWaysController.tsx:233-237). The zone is re-resolved by document.elementFromPoint on every move (19-22, 144-152). A pointer that leaves all zones is deleted and never re-tracked, because onPointerMove only handles known ids (238-240). Pressed state is painted by toggling .is-pressed without React re-renders (137-142).

CSS collision: pad.css defines .pad-modes twice (281 grid; 408 flex), and `.pad-modes button` / `.pad-modes button.is-on` (414-433) out-specify `.pad-mode` / `.pad-mode.is-on` (287-326), so the steering picker inherits the lobby game-mode button styles.

Tests run in Node via vitest, including only **/src/**/*.test.ts (vitest.config.ts). TS has noUncheckedIndexedAccess and noUnused* (tsconfig.base.json). ESLint uses typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked and eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7 recommended (eslint.config.js). dist/ and .vercel/ are gitignored.

The pad bundle must not pull in three.js: main.tsx lazy-loads routes so 'phones never download three.js' (client/src/main.tsx:7). The controller currently imports only inputSender, steering and itemIcons. config.ts has no imports.
risks: Double processing: if the pad applies dead zone and gamma to drag steer and the TV applies them again for every mode, the feel collapses near centre. Pick one place (recommended: the pad sends raw linear dx/travel, the TV shapes it, and the pad's ghost wheel previews it with the same shapeSteer function).

Analog throttle vs the strict `input.throttle === 0` reverse test (car.ts:390): tiny feathering residues block reverse and route into braking. Quantise and snap low values to 0 on the pad, use a threshold (< 0.05) on the TV, and never low-pass throttle on the TV.

GAS feathering ('slide down') moves the thumb off the pedal's bottom edge. With today's re-hit-test pointer model that releases the gas (SplitWaysController.tsx:144-152, 238-240). Steer and gas pointers need sticky roles. Rolling from GAS onto BRAKE should still switch, so define the precedence explicitly.

The 2 s 'Hold BRAKE to reverse' hint vs the 3 s auto stuck-respawn (config.ts:139, race.ts:215-228): the hint would show for ~1 s before a teleport. The reverse arming time (brake held at v≈0) also counts as 'stuck' today. Retune stuckSeconds or count gas-only stuck time. The autopilot full-race test depends on stuck respawn.

Rate-limit units: the spec says 120-180 deg/s and the research notes say road-wheel angle (with ~240°/s return). The current car rates are already road-wheel (3.4/5.5 rad/s ≈ 195/315°/s). At speed the lock is only 0.17 rad (9.7°), so the rate limit barely acts there and the 40 ms low-pass dominates. Don't add a second rate limiter on the normalised input as well.

Reverse-state latency: race status is 5 Hz on the reliable channel, so the ring/R chip/REVERSE label on the phone can lag up to 200 ms + RTT unless the TV pushes status the moment the reverse/hint state changes. Spamming sendRaceStatusTo must be throttled.
Pad bundle bloat: shared control helpers placed in or importing sim/, render/ or three would drag three.js/rapier into the phone chunk. Keep input/controls.ts dependency-free.
Node-only tests: device.ts registers a document listener at module load (device.ts:80), so any tested module that imports it fails in vitest. Keep the pure logic separate.

eslint-plugin-react-hooks v7 (compiler rules) flags reading ref.current during render and setState directly in effects. Keep pointer/drag state in refs that are touched only in handlers and the rAF tick, as the current code does.

iOS Safari: no Vibration API (visual feedback is the only channel), no element fullscreen on iPhone, and the system back-swipe from the left screen edge can fight a drag-steer zone that starts at the edge. Inset the zone by the safe area plus a margin. The wake lock still needs https, so the LAN self-signed cert flow stays.

Two-thumb limit: with drag steer on the left thumb, pressing HANDBRAKE with the right thumb drops GAS unless a throttle latch (slide from GAS onto the handbrake strip) is implemented. Removing tilt also takes away the hands-free horn-on-hub layout.

Keyboard players: gamma has no effect on digital ±1, but the new TV low-pass and slower rate limit change keyboard feel. Keep processing after mergeInputs so pad and keyboard on the same car share one filter state.

Reset abuse/races: manual Reset during respawn fade, after finishing, or spammed. Guard on phase === 'racing', finishedMs === null, respawn === 'none', and add a cooldown. A long-press on the phone avoids accidental resets. Don't map it to KeyR (debug resolution toggle when the overlay is open, game.ts:426).

Protocol drift: removing items/modes from protocol.ts (raceSchema item fields, actionSchema 'item', GAME_MODES/modeSchema, hapticSchema pickup/hit) touches hub.ts, TvApp.tsx, Lobby.tsx, LobbyScreen.tsx, SplitWaysStage.tsx (classic gating 115-116, 140) and the items cleanup owner's files. Coordinate so typecheck passes in one change.

Multi-pointer edge cases: a second finger landing in the steer zone, pointercancel from system gestures, or orientation change mid-drag (innerHeight changes the travel scale). Use the first steer pointer only and recompute travel at pointerdown.
